source.title: Report and Analysis of the P.R. Urban Elections in Ulster held on 15 January 1920 (Ulster Committee of the Proportional Representation Society of Ireland, 1920), Pottinger Ward results sheet; reprinted in PR Urban Elections in Ulster, 1920 (Electoral Reform Society, London, 1972), pp. 26-27, and the ward summary on p. 38
source.publisher: Proportional Representation Society of Ireland (Ulster Committee); reprinted by the Electoral Reform Society of Great Britain and Ireland
source.check: every stage transcribed by eye from the printed results sheet; every count adds to the printed valid vote, each result is the previous result plus the printed transfer, the quota is the valid vote divided by one more than the seats, plus one, and the party first-preference totals match the ward summary

note: First election by proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919, on the nine wards that replaced the fifteen of 1896. Polled 15 January 1920 and counted on 16 and 17 January. The ward returned 6 members: 1 alderman and 5 councillors.
boundaryNote: Pottinger electoral area: Pottinger ward. The nine electoral areas were constituted by the Local Government Board for Ireland's Order of 26 November 1919 (Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919, s. 1), adopting the Corporation's scheme of 4 August 1919, and are described in the same words as the nine Belfast divisions of the Redistribution of Seats (Ireland) Act 1918 (Second Schedule, Part I), so the map draws them from the 1918 parliamentary divisions. Sources: Belfast News-Letter, 6 August 1919, p. 6 (the scheme), and 19 December 1919, p. 11 (the Order).
